query: Israeli domestic politics August 2026: Is there a scheduled Knesset election? What is the state of Netanyahu's coalition (Smotrich, Ben Gvir) regarding the Board of Peace 15-point Gaza plan and withdrawal from Gaza? What political constraints affect Netanyahu accepting the plan before September 10, 2026?
answer:
I've submitted the structured findings. Summary of what the research established:

**The question's framing needs one correction:** there is no "coalition survival" problem, because there is no coalition left to collapse. The Knesset dissolved itself on 17 July 2026 and the election is locked to 27 October. Smotrich and Ben Gvir cannot bring the government down — what replaces that leverage is direct electoral competition for the same right-wing voters, plus formal legal restraints on what a caretaker government may decide.

**The strongest single piece of evidence** is Netanyahu's own reported words to Kushner on 17 August: progress on the 15-point framework is politically *"problematic"* ahead of 27 October. Reuters independently reports diplomats saying Israel is unlikely to make major concessions before the election, and the White House reportedly treats the rejections as campaign rhetoric.

**Three constraints I'd flag as under-appreciated:**

1. **The 24-hour trigger.** The roadmap annex requires withdrawal to the Yellow Line within 24 hours of government approval. Formal acceptance isn't a signing ceremony — it starts an immediate operational clock, which is why ministers specifically opposed even entering the 14-day preparatory period.
2. **The Attorney-General's election-period letter**, which requires legal pre-review of non-routine decisions and flags "signing of international agreements" for forthcoming guidelines. Procedural rather than absolute, but a real hurdle and a litigation hook.
3. **The precedent.** The Security Cabinet never formally adopted Trump's *original* 20-point plan either — Netanyahu endorsed it only in a personal statement, because of the statehood clause. The established pattern is approving narrow reversible components while withholding formal endorsement.

**Polling has severe house effects** — mainstream pollsters (Channel 12/13, Kan 11) put the Netanyahu bloc at 50–52; right-leaning ones (Channel 14, i24) at 58–63. The trend that matters: Otzma Yehudit rising 7→9→10 while Religious Zionism falls to 4, right at the threshold.

Two data-quality notes: AskNews returned 403 on this tier so all sourcing is web/Exa/direct fetch; and I discarded one search result citing a "September 8" trial resumption after checking it — that article is from 2025, not 2026. I found no external deadline tied to 10 September 2026; it appears to be the forecast horizon rather than a process milestone.

sources.title: Israel shifts right, but Netanyahu's coalition is losing ground: Here's why - analysis
sources.snippet: Aug 8, 2026. Between 15 and 25 mandates' worth of right-wing voters are currently unwilling to vote for any of the three existing right-wing parties: Likud, the Religious Zionist Party, and Otzma Yehudit.

key_facts: Israel's Knesset formally dissolved in the early hours of Friday 17 July 2026; Netanyahu voted in favour. The election is fixed for 27 October 2026 (results confirmed 4 November). This was the last possible date and made the 25th Knesset the first to serve a full four-year term since 1988.

Because the Knesset is already dissolved, Smotrich and Ben Gvir cannot bring down the government. The binding constraint has shifted from parliamentary arithmetic to electoral competition for the same right-wing voters.

Netanyahu told Kushner and Mladenov on 17 August 2026 that progress on the 15-point framework was politically 'problematic' ahead of the 27 October Knesset election, insisting Hamas take steps first (CNN via Times of Israel).

Netanyahu rejected the roadmap publicly on 4 August (Facebook video), 5 August (ruled out a Palestinian state), and definitively on 9 August at the Sunday cabinet meeting: 'Israel rejects the 15-point document. The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed... genuine disarmament, not a fictitious one.'

On 19 August 2026 an Israeli official contradicted the Board of Peace's upbeat account of the 17 August meeting, saying 'no progress was achieved during the talks' and the IDF will not withdraw from the October ceasefire demarcation line.

The 17 August 2026 four-hour Kushner-Netanyahu meeting produced only two working groups (disarmament/demilitarisation; sanitation/public health). A senior Israeli official could not provide the composition, precise role, or timeline for their establishment.

Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara wrote to ministers after dissolution: election-period restrictions now apply, ministers must exercise 'considerable restraint' in substantive decisions, and any non-routine decision requires preliminary legal review. She announced forthcoming guidelines explicitly covering 'signing of international agreements.'
Ben Gvir publicly dismissed the Attorney-General's letter, saying he never respected her authority and vowing to seek her dismissal in the next Knesset term.

The roadmap annex (seen by BBC) requires Israeli forces to withdraw to the Yellow Line 'within 24 hours of the Israeli government's approval of the plan' — formal approval is operationally immediate, not symbolic.

Roadmap point 2 requires the Phase 2 implementation timetable to be prepared within 14 days of approval by all parties. Cabinet ministers broadly opposed entering that 14-day period because it would restrict IDF operations including targeted strikes.

Mainstream polls (Channel 12, Channel 13, Kan 11) consistently put the Netanyahu bloc at 50-52 seats, short of the 61 needed. Right-leaning pollsters (Channel 14, i24/Direct Polls) show 58-63 — a large house effect, not movement.
Otzma Yehudit is gaining in mainstream polls: 7 seats (3 Aug) to 9 (5 Aug) to 10 (17 Aug), directly harvesting Likud defectors.
Religious Zionism has fallen to 4 seats in the Kan 11 poll of 17 August, the bare minimum to enter the Knesset. Ynet (27 July 2026) reported Smotrich and the RZP face 'an uphill fight for survival.'
Jerusalem Post analysis (8 Aug 2026) estimates 15-25 mandates' worth of right-wing voters are unwilling to vote for any of Likud, RZP, or Otzma Yehudit.

Likud won 32 seats in 2022 but polls at around 23 now. Netanyahu controls 8 reserved slots on the list and used one to endorse former Otzma Yehudit MK Almog Cohen at #8 — described by an analyst as an attempt to hold back Likud voters who defected to Ben Gvir.

At the 6 August Security Cabinet, IDF MI Research chief Brig. Gen. Ofir Mizrahi Rosen and Shin Bet Director David Zini warned that Hamas's acceptance of the roadmap is a 'strategic ambush' / attempt to 'trap Israel', explicitly tied to the 27 October elections.

The Security Cabinet never formally adopted Trump's original 20-point plan either. Netanyahu endorsed it only in a 'personal statement' alongside Trump, because of internal opposition to the Palestinian statehood clause.

On 26 July 2026 the Security Cabinet approved in principle ISF entry (~200 troops), granted ISF immunity, and approved the BoP Rafah pilot. Ben Gvir voted against; Smotrich voted in favour, then reversed on 3 August and demanded a revote.
The formal ISF agreement was never signed — the government secretary confirmed this on 6 August 2026.

Eight substantive gaps separate Trump's 20-point plan from the BoP roadmap, including weapons being 'held, stored or controlled' by NCAG rather than destroyed, governance under 'Palestinian laws', statehood as an explicit end goal, and the absence of the word 'terrorism' from the roadmap.
